name: Bronzes, Pages and Drumbeats: Africa's Creative Voices
description: Cities of learning, royal bronzes, Nobel writers, Afrobeat and Nollywood: a tour of the arts of Africa from medieval Cairo to the present.

checkpoints.name: Cities, kings and craft
checkpoints.note: Cairo is founded in 969, and Timbuktu grows into a trading and learning centre. The rock-cut churches of Lalibela are carved in Ethiopia in the 1200s, the Mali Empire rises from 1226 and Mansa Musa's famous pilgrimage carries its fame abroad. The Benin Bronzes are cast for the kings of Benin, and Kente cloth is woven in Ghana.

checkpoints.name: Pan-African currents
checkpoints.note: Pan-Africanism takes shape as a movement in 1900, and the Great Mosque of Djenné is rebuilt in mud brick in 1907. The writers and musicians who will make their names later are born: Naguib Mahfouz in 1911, Chinua Achebe in 1930, Miriam Makeba in 1932, Wole Soyinka in 1934 and Fela Kuti in 1938.

checkpoints.name: Independence and new art
checkpoints.note: Achebe's Things Fall Apart appears in 1958, and many African countries win independence around 1960. Black Girl (1966) is an early landmark of African cinema, Touki Bouki follows in 1973, and Fela Kuti builds Afrobeat in Nigeria in the late 1960s, releasing Zombie in 1977 as a sharp attack on soldiers in power.

checkpoints.name: Prizes and Nollywood
checkpoints.note: Wole Soyinka wins the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986, the first Black African writer to do so, and Naguib Mahfouz follows in 1988 as the first Arab laureate. Nollywood, Nigeria's fast-moving video film industry, begins in the 1990s, while Miriam Makeba, who sang against apartheid, dies in 2008.
